title: The Last Upload
tagline: A founder is found dead the morning after her launch party.
intro: Saturday, 07:40. Mara Quinn, 34, founder of the start-up Loopwire, is found dead on the floor of her apartment at 18 Larch Street, the morning after her company's launch party.
First officers call it an accident: too much wine, a fall, her head against the coffee table. Something about it bothers you.
Search the apartment. Unlock her devices. Talk to the four people who saw her last. When you are sure, name who killed her, how, and why.

locations.name: Living room
locations.description: Low light, a rug pulled out of place, the coffee table with a dark stain on its corner.

hotspots.info: The chalk outline where Mara was found, next to the chipped corner of the coffee table. The yellow markers number what the police noted: blood by her head, the rug, the table corner and her slippers.
hotspots.label: Chalk outline
hotspots.closeup: Where Mara was found. The corner of the coffee table is chipped and stained. Her slippers are side by side, neatly, a metre away. People who fall don't usually step out of their slippers first.

hotspots.info: An open bottle of red with barely one glass gone, and a single wine glass wiped completely clean: not one fingerprint, not even Mara's.
hotspots.label: Wine bottle
hotspots.closeup: An open bottle of red, barely a glass gone. The single glass beside it has been wiped so clean there isn't a fingerprint on it — not even Mara's.

hotspots.info: The bowl by the front door: loose coins and a spare key ring with a tag marked 'T'.
hotspots.label: Key bowl
hotspots.closeup: A ceramic bowl by the door. Among the coins: a spare key on a tag marked 'T'.

hotspots.info: A card Mara wrote for her mum's 60th birthday, Sunday 12 April. She never sent it.
hotspots.label: Birthday card
hotspots.closeup: A card on the shelf: 'Happy 60th, Mum! Sunday 12 April — love, Mara.' A copy she never sent?

hotspots.info: Left: the front of the Loopwire launch invitation. Right: the back, in Mara's handwriting: 'Talk to N. after!!'
hotspots.label: Invitation
hotspots.closeup: A thick card: 'Loopwire — Launch Night. Friday 19:00, The Glasshouse.' On the back, in Mara's hand: 'Talk to N. after!!'

hotspots.info: Mara's own slippers, paired neatly a metre from the body, as if someone placed them there.
hotspots.label: Slippers
hotspots.closeup: Mara's slippers, pink and grey, set neatly side by side a metre from where she lay. Nobody trips and falls out of their slippers this tidily.

hotspots.info: The shared family tablet, left on the sofa. Pick it up to look inside.
hotspots.label: Tablet on the sofa
hotspots.closeup: A family tablet in a scuffed case, left on the sofa cushions.

locations.name: Kitchen
locations.description: Clean, almost too clean. A kettle, still half full. Sticky notes everywhere.

hotspots.info: Left cup: rinsed clean. Right cup: a pale, chalky ring at the bottom, something that didn't dissolve in the tea.
hotspots.label: Sink
hotspots.closeup: Two tea cups in the sink. One has been rinsed. The other still has a pale, chalky ring at the bottom, like something didn't dissolve.

hotspots.info: Mara's sticky notes. The big yellow one says the laptop code is her mum's birthday, written day first, then month.
hotspots.label: Sticky notes
hotspots.closeup: Dozens of notes on the fridge. Groceries, a dentist reminder, and one in capitals: 'LAPTOP = MUM'S BIRTHDAY (day + month)'.

hotspots.info: A box of chamomile among Mara's usual green tea, with a Corner Pharmacy price sticker. It isn't her tea.
hotspots.label: Tea box
hotspots.closeup: An open box of chamomile tea. Every other tea in the cupboard is the same green tea brand. This one has a price sticker: 'Corner Pharmacy — open 24h'.

locations.name: Bedroom
locations.description: The bed hasn't been slept in. A phone face down on the nightstand.

hotspots.info: Mara's phone, face down on the nightstand, 12% battery left.
hotspots.label: Phone on nightstand

hotspots.info: The bed is made and the covers are untouched: Mara never went to sleep.
hotspots.label: Bed
hotspots.closeup: The bed is perfectly made. The covers haven't been turned back. Mara never went to bed last night.

hotspots.info: Mara's prescription sleeping tablets: 30 refilled eight days ago, only 4 left.
hotspots.label: Pill bottle
hotspots.closeup: Prescription sleeping pills in Mara's name, refilled eight days ago. Thirty tablets. Four are left.

locations.name: Office
locations.description: A desk facing the window, a laptop, a wall of books.

hotspots.info: Mara's laptop on her desk, locked.
hotspots.label: Laptop
hotspots.closeup: Mara's laptop, lid closed, still plugged in.

hotspots.info: The office alarm keypad. The buttons 0, 2 and 9 are worn shiny from daily use.
hotspots.label: Alarm keypad
hotspots.closeup: The office alarm keypad. Four buttons are worn shiny: 0, 2, 2 — no — 0, 2 and 9. Someone presses the same code a lot.

hotspots.info: Bank statements hidden behind the books. Yellow rows are transfers to an account ending 7731. Red note in Mara's hand: 'N. signs off all payments. Since March.'
hotspots.label: Behind the books
hotspots.closeup: Behind a row of paperbacks: a folder of printed bank statements. Fourteen transfers to an account ending 7731 are highlighted in yellow. In the margin: 'N. signs off all payments. Since March.'

locations.name: Nina's flat

suspects.name: Daniel Reyes
suspects.bio: Built Loopwire with Mara five years ago. Wanted to sell; she didn't.

questions.text: Where were you last night?
questions.answer: At the party until it closed, then the bar on Kemp Street with our investors until one, maybe later. Ask anyone there.
questions.summary: Claims: party, then Kemp Street bar with investors until ~01:00.

questions.text: How were things between you and Mara?
questions.answer: We disagreed about selling. Fine. But we'd agreed: no talking to buyers for a year. That was the deal, and I kept it.
questions.summary: Says they agreed not to talk to buyers for a year — and that he kept to it.

questions.text: When did you last speak to her?
questions.answer: I called her around quarter past ten. We argued — about the company, nothing personal. She hung up on me.
questions.summary: Called her ~22:15, argued about the company, she hung up.

questions.text: Ask about the 22:14 call
questions.answer: Six minutes of her telling me I was a traitor for even thinking about the offer. Then I left her a voicemail later to apologise. I was at the bar — you can hear it.
questions.summary: Confirms the 22:14 argument; points to his later voicemail from the bar.

questions.text: Who could approve payments from the company account?
questions.answer: Mara and... Nina. Nina did everything for her — payroll, vendors, all of it. I never touched the money side.
questions.summary: Only Mara and Nina could approve payments.

questions.text: Confront: the Halvorsen Capital email
questions.answer: ...Okay. Yes. I talked to a buyer behind her back. That makes me a bad partner, not a killer. I was at Kemp Street all night — there are cameras, there are twenty witnesses.
questions.summary: ADMITS secret sale talks with Halvorsen Capital. Insists on his bar alibi.

questions.text: Is there anything you haven't told me?
questions.answer: Mara deleted messages when she was angry. Every time. But she never emptied the bin — drove the IT guy mad.
questions.summary: Lead: Mara deleted angry messages but never emptied 'Recently deleted'.

questions.text: Who would know about her evening?
questions.answer: Nina. Her phone never leaves her hand. If anyone knows where Mara was every minute, it's Nina.
questions.summary: Lead: Nina's phone would tell Mara's evening.

questions.text: Is there anything you haven't told me?
questions.answer: Nina's gone. Not answering. Whatever she left in that flat, look at it properly.
questions.summary: Lead: search Nina's flat properly.

suspects.name: Theo Lambert
suspects.bio: Dated Mara for four years. They broke up two months ago.

questions.text: Where were you last night?
questions.answer: Home. Alone. All evening. So no alibi — great.
questions.summary: Claims: home alone all evening.

questions.text: Why did you break up?
questions.answer: Her choice. Work came first, always. I wasn't fine with it. But I'd never hurt her.
questions.summary: Mara ended it; he resented her work.

questions.text: Did she have enemies?
questions.answer: Last time we spoke she said someone at work was 'lying to her face every day'. She wouldn't say who.
questions.summary: Mara said someone at work was lying to her.

questions.text: Confront: your message at 22:31
questions.answer: Fine! I went by to drop off her key. Two minutes, I didn't even sit down. And when I came out — Nina was coming up the street with a paper bag. Twenty to eleven, roughly.
questions.summary: ADMITS dropping the key ~22:31–22:38. Saw NINA arriving with a paper bag ~22:40.

questions.text: Is there anything you haven't told me?
questions.answer: She wrote everything down. Passwords, codes, lists. Sticky notes all over the kitchen. Drove me mad.
questions.summary: Lead: Mara wrote codes on sticky notes in the kitchen.

suspects.name: Nina Shaw
suspects.bio: Worked for Mara for three years. Handles her diary, email and payments.
suspects.absentText: Nina Shaw cannot be found. Her phone is off. She has not been seen since last night.

questions.text: Where were you last night?
questions.answer: At the party until midnight, then straight home. I posted about it — you can check.
questions.summary: Claims: at the party until midnight, then home.

questions.text: What was Mara like as a boss?
questions.answer: Demanding. Fair. Three years... I loved that job. I still can't believe it.
questions.summary: Says she loved the job.

questions.text: When did you last see her?
questions.answer: At the party. She left around ten; she looked tired. That was the last time.
questions.summary: Says she last saw Mara at the party ~22:00.

questions.text: Ask about the flagged transfers
questions.answer: I process hundreds of payments a month. If something's wrong it's a vendor error. Daniel set most of those accounts up anyway.
questions.summary: Blames vendor error and Daniel for the 7731 transfers.

questions.text: Can I see your phone?
questions.answer: ...Sure. Of course. I've got nothing to hide.
questions.summary: Handed over her phone.

questions.text: Confront: the photo of you leaving at 22:16
questions.answer: Okay — I left early. I needed air. I walked around. That's all. I just didn't want to explain.
questions.summary: Changes story: left the party at 22:16 'to walk around'.

questions.text: Confront: your location at Larch Street, 22:40–23:24
questions.answer: ...She asked me to come. We had tea. We talked about work. We argued, a bit. But she was alive when I left. I swear she was alive.
questions.summary: Changes story AGAIN: was at Mara's 22:40–23:24, made tea, argued. Claims Mara was alive when she left.

questions.text: Confront: your search at 22:03
questions.answer: You're reading my searches now? I can't sleep, okay? I was looking it up for ME. This is insane.
questions.summary: ANGRY. Claims the sleeping-pill search was for herself.

suspects.name: Walter Briggs
suspects.bio: Lives next door in 4A. Has complained about noise from Mara's flat many times.

questions.text: Where were you last night?
questions.answer: Home. I'm always home. Television, then bed at half past ten.
questions.summary: Home all night, in bed by 22:30.

questions.text: Did you hear anything?
questions.answer: Nothing. Slept like a log.
questions.summary: Claims he heard nothing.

questions.text: How did you get on with Mara?
questions.answer: She had parties. I complained. Is that a crime now?
questions.summary: Noise complaints against Mara.

questions.text: Confront: your post about shouting at 11pm
questions.answer: All right. All right. Two women, shouting, around eleven. One of them said 'You'll ruin me.' Then it went quiet. I didn't want to get involved.
questions.summary: ADMITS hearing two women argue ~23:00: 'You'll ruin me.'

questions.text: Did you see anyone?
questions.answer: Through the peephole. Twenty past eleven, maybe. A young woman, dark coat, paper bag, in a hurry. Not the girlfriend type — she looked like she worked for someone.
questions.summary: Saw a young woman in a dark coat with a paper bag leave ~23:20.

questions.text: Is there anything you haven't told me?
questions.answer: I... might have written something on the building's page. About the noise. People get worked up online.
questions.summary: Lead: he posted about the noise on the building's social page.

how.label: Pushed during an argument; hit her head on the table
Sleeping pills crushed into her tea, then staged as a fall

why.label: To force through the sale of the company
To stop her reporting the stolen money

hints.who: Check every alibi against the phones. Who said they were somewhere else, and what do the photos, messages and location history say?
hints.how: Forget the fall for a moment. Look at what Mara drank that night, and at what was missing from her bedroom.
hints.why: Follow the money. What did Mara learn at 18:05, and who was she seeing at 9:00 the next morning?

solved.title: Case closed
text: Nina Shaw is arrested. Faced with the location history, the search and the second cup, she stops talking. Then, very quietly, she starts again.

"She found out at six. She texted me 'I know'. I thought if she just slept... I crushed her pills into the tea. When she went down, I panicked. I made it look like a fall. I wiped the glass. I wiped everything."
Mara Quinn had a lawyer's appointment at nine. She never made it.

released.title: Released for lack of proof
text: You have the right person — but the case doesn't hold. The prosecutor sends it back: the method or the motive isn't proven by the evidence you attached.
The suspect walks out of the station. Rebuild the case and try again.

escaped.title: The killer got away
text: Another wrong arrest. By the time the truth comes out, Nina Shaw is on a one-way flight to Lisbon.
Mara's family will get answers. They won't get justice.

solution: How: she crushed Mara's own sleeping pills into chamomile tea she brought over, then staged a fall against the coffee table and wiped the glass.
Why: she had stolen £86,400 from Loopwire. Mara found out from the bank at 18:05 and was seeing a lawyer the next morning.

twist.title: The killer moves again
text: While you were busy with the wrong suspect, someone used the assistant login to wipe Mara's laptop remotely at 03:12. Everything still on it is gone — only what you already took is safe.
This morning Nina Shaw did not show up. Her phone is off. Officers have opened her flat. A new location is available.
